name_story.story: Asem can be understood through the Arabic form عَاصِم, whose central sense is asem; protector, guardian. Asem is Arabic عَاصِم (ʿĀṣim), the active participle of عَصَمَ, meaning 'protector, guardian'.

faq.a: Asem is associated with the Arabic form عَاصِم, whose core sense is asem; protector, guardian.

faq.q: What is the origin of Asem?
faq.a: Asem is associated with Arabic. Asem is Arabic عَاصِم (ʿĀṣim), the active participle of عَصَمَ, meaning 'protector, guardian'.
Yes — the underlying form عَاصِم is Arabic.
Asem can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Asem should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. The root ع ص م is Quranic, but ʿĀṣim is not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Asem mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Asem is rendered عاصم and carries the sense عاصم، محافظ.

faq.q: What does Asem mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Asem is rendered عاصم and carries the sense عاصم، نگهبان.
A romanized syllable approximation is a-sem. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Asem?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Asem, asem. Script forms are عاصم, عَاصِم, आसिम.

faq.q: Is Asem a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
